title: From Production Chemistry to Interfacial Reactions: Low- and Moderate-Temperature Biochar and Hydrochar for Integrated Wastewater Treatment
authors: B. Kayan and A. Alver · Reactions
abstract: This critical review examines the potential of low- and moderate-temperature biochar and hydrochar for wastewater treatment, emphasizing the relationship between production conditions, surface chemistry, and contaminant removal. Particular attention is given to materials produced at temperatures up to 250°C and their comparison with higher-temperature derivatives. The review highlights the roles of surface functional groups, mineral interactions, and organic domains in removing metals and organic pollutants. It also evaluates the effects of feedstock characteristics, water chemistry, material modification, and regeneration on treatment performance. Key challenges include long-term stability, sorbent reuse, and limited engineering-scale evidence. The study emphasizes the need for reliable performance, cost, and environmental assessments before practical implementation.
